⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

I visited Bangbae Jjok Galbi a few days ago, and it was a truly satisfying experience. It is located a 5-minute walk from Bangbae Station, making it highly accessible and easy to find. The inside of the store is neat and cozy, making it the perfect place for family gatherings or meetings with friends.

We chose spicy seasoned ribs and regular seasoned ribs for one person each, and added cheese and rice balls. The spiciness was not irritating, but it left a spicy kick on the tip of the tongue, making it worth a try even for those who are not good at eating spicy food. In particular, adding cheese gently neutralized the spiciness and added a nutty flavor, making it a truly fantastic combination. The regular flavor was a sweet and salty flavor that anyone could enjoy, and the freshness of the meat made me admire it every time I ate it.

It wasn't just the meat that was good. The rice balls added as a side dish were lightly grilled on the grill, so they were crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, making them a delicacy. I also ate soybean paste stew and steamed egg, and I was very satisfied as I was able to end my meal with a satisfying meal.

The staff kindly grilled the meat and gave detailed instructions on how to eat it, so even beginners could easily enjoy it. Since I was able to freely refill side dishes at the self-service bar, I was able to finish my meal without missing anything.

I especially liked that Bangbae Jjok Galbi uses domestically produced jjang ribs and offers a fresh and reliable taste. It's a great place to eat at Bangbae Station, so I plan to visit again with my family next time. I was completely satisfied with the quality of the meat, the taste of the seasoning, and the friendly service.

If you are looking for a delicious meat restaurant near Bangbae Station, I would definitely recommend Bangbae Jjok Galbi. 😊

reviews.text: I don't prefer regular meat, but I really like ribs with bones. As much as I like it, I'm picky about the quality. Bangbae jjok ribs were delicious steamed ribs. It was also attractive that they used only domestically produced back ribs and had no unpleasant odor at all. The smoke flavor was properly coated in the meat, and the subtle fire flavor was amazing. The salt ribs and seasoned ribs were so perfect that I had nothing to say about them, and the unique ribs (kanpung ribs) were also attractive. Kkanpung Jjanggalbi was a dish that combined the flavors of Chinese and Korean food and had a characteristic sweet yet spicy taste. It also had a slight crispiness, so it was a dish that combined the feeling and sensibility of Kkanpung-style ribs. And the side dish here, octopus ramen, is a must-try. There was a whole octopus in it, and the owner, who has a great knowledge of noodles, cooked it with the golden ratio of water and soup, making it an incredible ramen that cannot be imitated at home. I've been to this friendly and charming side rib restaurant in Naebang Station for a day now as my best friend.

Unlike most ramen restaurants, the noodles were slightly thicker, closer to Chinese noodles, but the texture was surprisingly good, the broth was very clean, and the toppings were good. Instead of bamboo shoots, there was roasted lotus root on top, which was different and nice. The best advantage is that you can add noodles for free. You can choose yuzu kosho, but I personally found the yuzu flavor to be too strong, ruining the clean soup, which was a bit disappointing. The quantity of karaage was small, but since it was not frozen, it was soft and tasty. One thing that is a bit unfortunate is that there is a wait, but it is not a wait because the business is doing too well, but because the food comes out too late. It's understandable since you work alone in the kitchen, but it still takes a long time to come out. One part-time worker felt like he was confused and there was something disorganized. reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
On the way to Mandarin, Adam Dumpling caught my eye and I remembered it. After eating sweet and sour pork at Mandarin, I decided to stop by.

Although Mandarin's sweet and sour pork is small, it has a good volume. I was full after eating it all, but I wanted to stop by at least one more place, so I stopped by Adam Mandu.

People passing by seemed to be curious as to whether it was a new product or not, so I looked at the menu and saw that there were rolled dumplings with thin dumpling skin, dumplings that used to be called whole dumplings, which I like, and Chinese-style king dumplings. Since I'm mostly a dumpling fan, I asked if it was possible to order meat dumplings and kimchi dumplings half and half. I'm just as curious as the meat dumplings, so I have no choice but to ask for one of each.

After putting the already made gyoza dumplings on the steamer, the young clerks at the front of the store take care of packaging and checkout, while an older person inside continues to make the dumplings.

Finally, the meat dumplings and kimchi dumplings were packaged, and as a service, they also packaged meat dumplings and kimchi dumplings and added them as well.

When I brought it home and unpacked it, there were things like pickled radish, soy sauce, and wooden chopsticks packaged together. When I tasted the pickled radish first, I found that most modern dumpling places tend to have the thin and sweet type, but this place has the chewy and salty type.

When I first tasted the meat gyoza dumplings, the vegetables in them were reasonably crunchy and not particularly spicy, but they were good enough without any unpleasant smell. Even my young family members tasted them and liked them.

Depending on the store, the kimchi gyoza dumplings can be either plain enough that you don't know they're kimchi dumplings, or they can be very spicy. I was wondering if that was the case, and when I tasted it, the vegetables had the same crunchy texture, and it was a bit spicier than I prefer, so I felt a little embarrassed if it was spicy, but it wasn't too plain or too spicy, so it was okay.

When I was young, my mother liked it, so I occasionally tasted the meat dumplings sold at Chwicheonru in Myeongdong, which has now moved to Seochon. This restaurant's Wangmandu, which feels similar to a larger version, has the same dumpling filling as gyoza dumplings and a thicker dumpling skin, but I just prefer the gyoza dumpling type, so I don't think I'll order it on purpose.

Overall, on my way to taste sweet and sour pork at Mandarin, I was curious and stopped by. The dumplings I picked up and tasted were like the Ewha dumplings near Gunja Station, with a good volume and a moderately good taste. They weren't the type that made me feel special, so I didn't have to stop by far away, but I thought it was worth stopping by if I was nearby, and since it was a new store, I said it was delicious as a sign of support.

reviews.text:
The desserts and drinks are delicious and the staff are friendly and nice, but the store is very small. There are only two tables and you have to go outside and go down to the basement at the back of the building to use the bathroom, but the cell phone signal itself doesn't work and is blocked, so you can't make calls or get data at all. I was scared because it seemed dangerous and it was a dark basement.
I expected that the Yeonnam branch would close and the Bangbae branch would open in a better location, but it was disappointing in every way.
I ordered Gateau Basque Raspberry, Milk Tea Matcha Latte, Salted Caramel Financier, Blue Cheese Honey Financier, No. 73 Pistachio, Cherry Dessert, and White Mole Sweet Tea.
It was inconvenient to stay in the store. My hands got sticky after eating dessert and drinks, so I asked for wet wipes, but they only gave me a napkin, which made it difficult to wipe my sticky hands. The chairs were too shaky, the store was too small, and the moment I stayed was very uncomfortable, so I hurried to eat and went to the cafe next door. I tried to stay comfortably like I did at the Yeonnam branch, but it was disappointing. The taste of the dessert was so good that I'm only going to do take-out from now on. I think this is a fatal flaw for the store. I hope it improves in a better direction and has a long run. The desserts are so delicious
In the case of dessert number 73, it has a rich pistachio taste, the thin and crispy sandwiches on the top and bottom are delicious, and it is delicious no matter how many times you eat it, but the cherry jam inside is a bit unpleasant. It may be an artificial taste, but I think something other than the fishy sweetness of cherry would suit it. Still, it is delicious.
The blue cheese honey Finangsi was so sweet and salty that it was so delicious. The flavor of the blue cheese spreads in your mouth, and the Hinangsi is moist and not dry.
The salted caramel finangsi was the same moist finangsi with a hard caramel coating topped with salt, and the taste was just edible. It was delicious, but I was a little less impressed by the impact of the blue cheese finangsi.
What exceeded my expectations was the Gateau Basque Raspberry. It was a dessert with a crunchy cookie-like texture on the outside but a moist and soft inside like an egg tart, but the sour raspberry jam inside was not to my taste. The basic taste and texture were good, so I was curious about other flavors of Gateau Basque.
I think I should order takeout and eat it at home haha.
